selectedIdea.title: Een bemoedigende busproef is nog geen bewezen vlootbusinesscase
selectedIdea.description: Vertel wat de proef concreet opleverde en waarom service, metingen, toegankelijkheid en kosten elk hun eigen bewijsgrens hebben. De volgende beslissing betreft een winterbeoordeling.
selectedIdea.audience: Professionals die operationele pilotresultaten moeten beoordelen en uitleggen.
selectedIdea.rationale: Een concrete, brongetrouwe uitleg helpt het gerapporteerde resultaat te onderscheiden van een te sterke conclusie.
selectedIdea.evidence: De bron beschrijft een echte opbrengst binnen het fictieve dossier, aparte kwaliteitsdimensies, beperkingen van vergelijkingen en een beperkt vervolgbesluit.

research.content:
### Facts

1. HarborLink and this dossier are explicitly fictional; the dossier describes a synthetic evaluation, not a real transport study. (Section 1)
2. The demonstration ran 4 May–28 June; its comparison period ran 9 March–3 May. The final ledger records 2,240/2,400 completions (93.3%) for the six vehicles later displaced and 2,310/2,400 (96.3%) for the electric group. Completion uses the same definition in both periods. The draft’s 2,340 trial departures included 30 duplicate IDs, removed on 9 July. (Sections 1–2, “final dispatch ledger”)
3. The completion measure is service delivery, not exclusive electric operation: a diesel-substituted trip counted as a completed route departure but not as an electric-bus departure. (Section 3)
4. The displayed punctuality rates, 82% and 89%, use different lateness thresholds (three minutes versus five); old GPS records were not reprocessed to a common threshold. The source says the difference may combine service differences with this measurement change. (Section 2)
5. The electric buses were assigned non-randomly to two relatively flat routes near the depot; diesel buses retained a longer hill route. Those diesel buses’ completion rose from 1,170/1,200 to 1,188/1,200, while roadworks ended on part of that route in April. The dossier calls this contextual, not randomized, and says terrain and dispatch differences prevent a clean effect estimate. (Sections 1–2)
6. Accessibility checks found the specified wheelchair space on all three inspected buses, but two had audio-stop announcement failures; the third passed both checks. The two audio units were restored on 2 July, after the trial. Physical space and functioning announcements are separate dimensions. (Section 4)
7. Recorded electricity expenditure was EUR 8,400 under a temporary tariff; the six comparable diesel vehicles had previously used EUR 13,700 of fuel while driving 38,000 km versus 35,000 electric-bus km. The source notes different traffic and energy sources, excludes several charger and training costs from the electricity figure, and says no like-for-like whole-cost calculation was produced. The tariff expires 31 October. (Section 3)
8. The source says neither energy figure is a certified whole-life emissions estimate; manufacturing, battery replacement and grid-displacement analysis were not commissioned. It states that a net-carbon reduction is not demonstrated. (Section 3)
9. The demonstration had no freezing days or winter heating loads, and the leased buses had not been tested on the hill route in winter. The engineering team proposed a winter run with heating and matched route allocation. (Section 5)
10. On 18 September, the board authorized preparation of a winter-assessment specification within the existing planning budget. It did not authorize another lease, depot conversion or procurement award. The board rejected draft wording that the pilot had “proved the business case” and approved a description of “encouraging operational experience” with unresolved cost, seasonality and comparison questions. (Section 6)

### Unknowns

- Whether the higher recorded completion rate was caused by electric propulsion or would persist under comparable routes, dispatch and conditions is not established; the source identifies non-random assignment and contextual differences (Facts 2, 5).
- A comparable punctuality change under one threshold is unknown because the source provides no common-threshold reprocessing (Fact 4).
- Whole-cost savings, annual savings or fleet payback are unsupported: a like-for-like cost calculation was not produced and recorded expenditure omits costs and uses a temporary tariff (Fact 7).
- Net whole-life emissions impact is not established (Fact 8).
- Winter performance, heating energy needs and performance on the hill route remain untested; the winter run is a proposal, not a result (Fact 9).
- The source does not establish that the two repaired audio units remained functional in subsequent service or that all operating accessibility conditions were met beyond the three inspections (Fact 6).
